CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for reassessment of anxiety management, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, headache symptoms, and medication review.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting minimal improvement in his overall symptoms since the last visit. He has adhered to the sertraline regimen of 150 mg daily; however, he expresses concerns regarding persistent anxiety, particularly in the context of ongoing work-related pressures. He describes episodes of heightened anxiety occurring approximately 4-5 times per week, particularly before project deadlines, which he finds increasingly challenging to manage.
Sleep disturbances remain significant, with Mr. Smith reporting an average of 4-5 hours of sleep per night, frequently interrupted by anxiety-related ruminations. He continues to utilize cognitive-behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) techniques but admits that the benefits have been limited. He has also maintained his melatonin dosage at 5 mg at bedtime but feels it has not contributed meaningfully to improving his sleep quality.
Headaches have not changed in frequency, occurring 3-4 times per week, with a consistent intensity rated as moderate to severe. Mr. Smith notes that he has been using ibuprofen 400 mg approximately 3 times weekly for relief, reporting some efficacy but still experiencing significant discomfort during episodes. He continues to associate these headaches with his anxiety levels, but he has not noticed any new headache patterns or additional symptoms.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 150 mg daily 2. Melatonin 5 mg at bedtime 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 4. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief 5. Amitriptyline 5 mg nightly
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer and reports that work-related stressors have been exacerbated by recent project demands, leading to increased anxiety. He maintains a walking routine three times a week and engages in mindfulness meditation; however, he acknowledges difficulty in maintaining this practice during particularly stressful periods. He remains abstinent from alcohol and is focused on improving his lifestyle choices.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Ongoing anxiety with limited improvement; persistent sleep disturbances; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Persistent tension-type headaches as previously described; no visual changes or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue noted; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/76 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert and oriented, in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears anxious with fluctuations noted.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Given the persistence of anxiety symptoms, consider increasing sertraline to 200 mg daily. Discuss the potential addition of lorazepam for acute anxiety management during particularly stressful periods. 2. Insomnia: Continue melatonin at 5 mg at bedtime; reinforce CBT-I strategies. Referral for a sleep study is warranted to evaluate for possible obstructive sleep apnea due to ongoing sleep disturbances. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue ibuprofen as needed; consider increasing the dose of amitriptyline to 10 mg nightly for preventive therapy if headache frequency remains unchanged. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage continued engagement in physical activity and mindfulness practices; discuss potential dietary adjustments to enhance overall energy levels.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2027-06-01 to evaluate ongoing symptoms, assess treatment effectiveness, and make further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is advised to reach out to the office sooner if he experiences any worsening of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
